user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production
- Enforces consistent coding standards across the codebase
- Reduces technical debt over time

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads context** so no single person owns critical code
- Junior developers learn from senior feedback
- Everyone stays familiar with different parts of the project

## Risk Reduction
- **Reduces bus factor** — work isn't lost if someone leaves
- Provides a second set of eyes on security vulnerabilities
- Creates a natural checkpoint before merging changes

## Team Collaboration
- Encourages **open discussion** about design decisions
- Builds a shared sense of ownership and accountability
- Improves communication habits across the team

## Practical Tips for Small Teams
| Challenge | Solution |
|---|---|
| Limited reviewers | Rotate who reviews what |
| Slow turnaround | Set a 24-hour review SLA |
| Nitpicking | Use a linter to handle style automatically |

## Bottom Line
Even with just **2–3 people**, code review pays off by preventing costly mistakes, keeping everyone aligned, and building a stronger, more maintainable codebase — without requiring a formal process.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain a higher-quality, more maintainable codebase.

1. **Bug detection** — A second reviewer catches mistakes before they reach production, saving time and reducing costly fixes later.
2. **Knowledge sharing** — Team members stay familiar with each other's code, reducing dependency on any single person.
Code review builds a **shared sense of ownership**, encouraging team members to take collective responsibility for the quality of the codebase rather than treating code as individual territory.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If code reviews are skipped, **bugs and security vulnerabilities are more likely to slip into production**, potentially causing system failures or data breaches that are far more costly to fix after the fact.

Track **review turnaround time** — the average time between a pull request being opened and receiving feedback — to ensure reviews happen promptly and don't become a bottleneck in your development workflow.
Even a lightweight review process can make a significant difference in code quality and team cohesion.

• Code review improves quality, collaboration, and shared ownership.
• Skipping it risks bugs, vulnerabilities, and knowledge silos.
• Track turnaround time to keep the process efficient.
• Even a lightweight process delivers significant long-term value.
Code review is a simple practice with outsized benefits for any small team.
Code review is only effective if feedback is constructive and timely — poorly managed reviews can slow down development and damage team morale.
Bad reviews hurt teams; keep feedback kind, clear, and prompt.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only works well when feedback is timely, constructive, and consistent.
